title: Fall Pool Care and Maintenance Guide
summary: Before you start thinking about winter closing, use this in-between season to clean, inspect, balance, and tune up your pool.
body_markdown:
Summer may be winding down, but pool care season is not over yet. Fall is one of the most important times to give your pool a little extra attention, especially if you plan to close it for winter later in the season. Think of fall pool care as the bridge between summer maintenance and winter closing. It helps you clean up after a busy swim season, catch small equipment issues before they become bigger problems, and make sure your pool is in the best possible shape before it sits covered for the off-season.


## Fall Pool Care at a Glance


- Test and Balance
- Remove Debris
- Deep Clean the Pool
- Filter Care
- Equipment Tune-Ups
- Heater TLC
- Inspect Your Pool Cover
- Check Pool Tools
- Watch for Algae
- Keep the Pool Area Clear
- Plan for Closing
- Fall Pool Care Checklist


## Why Fall Pool Care Matters


After months of swimming, sun, storms, sunscreen, and heavy chemical demand, your pool has been through a lot. Even if the water still looks clear, there may be buildup in the filter, debris in the plumbing, worn equipment parts, or water balance issues that need attention.


Fall is also when leaves, dirt, and organic debris start making their way into the pool more often. If left untreated, this debris can clog baskets, strain the pump, stain pool surfaces, and feed algae growth. Staying ahead of these issues now can make closing easier and help prevent a green, messy pool when it’s time to reopen.


Before you start thinking about winter closing, use this in-between season to clean, inspect, balance, and tune up your pool.


## 1. Keep Testing and Balancing Your Water


Even if you’re swimming less, your pool still needs consistent water care. Cooler temperatures may slow algae growth, but they do not eliminate the need for proper chemistry. Rain, leaves, dirt, and changing weather can still throw your water out of balance.


**[Test your water](https://lesliespool.com/water-testing/)** regularly throughout the fall and **[adjust](https://lesliespool.com/water-balancers/)** as needed. Pay close attention to:


- **[Free chlorine](https://lesliespool.com/chlorine/)**
- **[pH](https://lesliespool.com/ph/)**
- **[Total alkalinity](https://lesliespool.com/alkalinity/)**
- **[Calcium hardness](https://lesliespool.com/calcium-hardness/)**
- **[Cyanuric acid](https://lesliespool.com/stabilizer-conditioner/)**
- **[Phosphates](https://lesliespool.com/phosphate-remover/)**
- **[Metals](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-nometal-metal-stain-remover-1l/18836.html)**


Balanced water helps protect pool surfaces, prevent scaling or staining, and keep your sanitizer working properly. This is especially important before closing, because any water chemistry problems left untreated can get worse while the pool is covered.


For the most accurate results, bring a water sample to your **[local Leslie’s](https://lesliespool.com/stores)** for a free water test. You’ll get a complete 10-point water analysis and a customized treatment plan to help keep your pool clear and protected.


**PRO TIP** : Need a refresher on how to balance your pool water? Check out this **[helpful blog article](https://lesliespool.com/blog/how-to-balance-pool-water.html)** for all the information you need to keep your pool water chemistry balanced.


## 2. Clean Up Leaves and Debris Often


Fall leaves may look beautiful on trees, but they are not great for your pool. Leaves and organic debris can quickly use up your chlorine, clog baskets, overload your filter, and leave stains on your pool surface.


**[Skim](https://lesliespool.com/pool-rakes-skimmers-nets/)** the pool often, especially after windy days or storms. Empty skimmer and pump baskets regularly so water can flow properly through the system. If your pool is surrounded by trees, consider using a **[leaf net](https://lesliespool.com/18-pro-grade-leaf-rake/82627.html)** or automatic pool cleaner to stay ahead of the mess.


You should also **[brush](https://lesliespool.com/pool-brushes/)** the walls, steps, ladders, and corners of the pool. Debris and algae love to settle in areas with poor circulation, so brushing helps keep surfaces clean and gives your sanitizer a better chance to do its job.


**DID YOU KNOW?** : The **[Betta SE Plus](https://lesliespool.com/betta-se-plus-solar-powered-smart-robotic-pool-skimmer-2-year-warranty/34208.html)** is the ultimate fall pool care sidekick. With over 30 hours of cleaning and an XL debris basket, this solar-powered robotic skimmer makes it easier than ever to keep leaves and other fall debris out of your pool.


## 3. Vacuum and Deep Clean the Pool


Fall is a good time to give your pool a more thorough cleaning after a busy summer. **[Vacuum](https://lesliespool.com/pool-vacuum-heads/)** the floor to remove dirt, leaves, and fine debris that may have settled below the surface. Pay extra attention to steps, benches, corners, and the deep end.


If you notice stains from leaves or other organic material, treat them with **[Leslie's Stain & Scale Remover](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-pool-stain-scale-remover-1-2-gallon/18399.html)** before closing. Organic stains are often easier to remove when they are fresh. Waiting until spring can make the problem harder to fix.


This is also a great time to clean the waterline, tile, ladders, handrails, and other pool surfaces. Removing buildup now helps prevent grime, scale, and residue from sitting on your pool all winter.


## 4. Clean and Inspect Your Filter


Your filter worked hard all summer, and fall is the perfect time to clean it thoroughly. A dirty or worn filter can reduce circulation, make it harder to maintain clear water, and put extra strain on your pool equipment.


For cartridge filters, rinse and **[clean](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-cartridge-cleaner-1-qt./14225.html)** the cartridges thoroughly. Look for cracked end caps, torn pleats, fraying, flattened folds, or cartridges that no longer come clean. If they look worn or damaged, **[replace them](https://lesliespool.com/filter-cartridges/)** .


For D.E. filters, backwash if needed, then inspect the **[grids](https://lesliespool.com/de-filter-grids/)** for tears, cracks, or buildup. If your filter needs a deeper clean, this is a good time to take care of it before cooler weather sets in.


For sand filters, backwash when the pressure rises 8–10 psi above the clean starting pressure or according to the manufacturer’s guidelines. If your sand is several years old and filtration has become less effective, it may be time to **[replace the filter sand](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-natural-zeolite-pool-filter-sand-25-lbs/18824.html)** .


## 5. Schedule an Equipment Tune-Up


Fall is one of the best times to inspect and service your pool equipment. After a long summer of heavy use, your pump, filter, heater, heat pump, valves, automation, and plumbing may need attention.


Check your **[pool parts](https://lesliespool.com/pool-parts/)** for leaks, unusual noises, poor water flow, air bubbles, worn **[O-rings](https://lesliespool.com/pool-o-ring-kits/)** , cracked lids, loose fittings, and changes in pressure. Small issues can turn into expensive repairs if they are left untreated through the off-season. This is especially important if you plan to close your pool for winter. Equipment problems are much easier to fix before closing than after freezing temperatures arrive or when you’re ready to reopen in spring.


If something seems off, **[schedule a professional inspection](https://lesliespool.com/service)** with Leslie’s. Our pool experts can help identify worn parts, performance issues, and potential repairs before they become bigger headaches.


## 6. Give Heaters and Heat Pumps Extra Attention


If you have a **[pool heater](https://lesliespool.com/pool-heaters/)** or **[heat pump](https://lesliespool.com/pool-heat-pumps/)** , fall maintenance is especially important. These systems often get used more as the weather cools down, and they need to be in good condition to perform safely and efficiently.


Before relying on your heater for fall swimming, check that it starts properly, heats consistently, and has good water flow. Clear leaves, dirt, and debris away from the unit, and make sure the surrounding area is open and well-ventilated.


For gas heaters, watch for signs of trouble like unusual smells, ignition problems, error codes, sooting, rust, or inconsistent heating. If you have a heat pump, look for blocked airflow, debris around the coils, strange noises, or reduced heating performance. For more information about heat pump care and troubleshooting, check out this **[article](https://lesliespool.com/blog/pool-heat-pump-troubleshooting-guide.html)** !


A professional heater or heat pump **[tune-up](https://lesliespool.com/service)** can help improve efficiency, extend equipment life, and make sure everything is ready before closing. It can also help catch issues before the spring rush, when service appointments may be harder to schedule.


## 7. Inspect Your Pool Cover Before You Need It


Don’t wait until closing day to find out your **[pool cover](https://lesliespool.com/pool-covers/)** is damaged! Fall is the right time to inspect your cover, hardware, and accessories so you have enough time to repair or replace anything that needs attention.


Lay out your pool cover and check for:


- Tears, holes, or fraying
- Worn straps or broken buckles
- Missing or damaged springs
- Bent or loose anchors
- Weak seams
- Stretched or sagging areas
- Excessive mildew or buildup


If you use a solid cover, inspect the **[cover pump](https://lesliespool.com/pool-cover-pumps/)** and make sure it works properly. If you use a safety cover, check that the **[anchors](https://lesliespool.com/pool-cover-hardware-parts/)** and hardware are in good condition.


Cleaning your cover before installation also helps reduce dirt, debris, and contaminants around the pool. If your cover is damaged, repair or replace it before closing. A properly fitting, well-maintained cover helps protect your pool from debris, sunlight, and harsh winter conditions.


**PRO TIP** : If your pool cover has some minor damage, don't despair, just repair! Mild tearing, wonky anchors, and other superficial damage can oftentimes be fixed with just a few tools. Check out this **[helpful article](https://lesliespool.com/blog/how-to-repair-a-pool-cover.html)** for more information.


## 8. Check Pool Accessories and Maintenance Tools


Fall is also a good time to inspect the **[tools](https://lesliespool.com/pool-maintenance/)** and accessories you use all season long. Check your skimmer net, brush, pole, vacuum head, hose, test kit, baskets, thermometer, and cleaner parts.


Replace anything that is cracked, torn, missing bristles, difficult to adjust, or no longer working properly. Having reliable tools on hand makes fall cleanup easier and helps you avoid scrambling for replacements when you’re ready to close.


Clean and dry pool toys, floats, ladders, handrails, and removable accessories before storing them. This helps prevent mildew, fading, cracking, and chemical damage during the off-season.


## 9. Watch for Algae, Even in Cooler Weather


Algae is more common in warm weather, but fall pools are not immune. Leaves, rain, low sanitizer, poor circulation, and unbalanced water can all create the right conditions for algae growth.


Keep **[chlorine](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-3-inch-jumbo-chlorine-pool-tablets-35-lbs-bucket/18743.html)** at the proper level, brush regularly, run your pump long enough for good circulation, and remove debris quickly. If your pool has recurring algae issues, use an algaecide or phosphate remover, like **[Leslie's No Phos](https://lesliespool.com/leslies-nophos-phosphate-remover-3l-bottle/18835.html)** , as part of your fall pool care routine.


The cleaner and more balanced your pool is before closing, the better chance you have of opening to clear water in spring.


**PRO TIP:** Algae removal is easier when you have the right products on hand. **[Leslie’s Algae Removal Bundles](https://lesliespool.com/algae-control/)** and **[Algae Cleanup Bundles](https://lesliespool.com/green-to-clean-4-lb-with-power-powder-plus-pool-shock-25-lb.-bucket-and-clear-aid-2l-bundle/B-2134.html)** include the key products you need to treat green, yellow, or black algae and help bring your pool water back to clear.


## 10. Trim Nearby Trees and Clean the Pool Area


Your fall pool care routine should include the area around the pool, too. Trim overhanging branches, sweep the deck, clear leaves from nearby landscaping, and remove loose debris that could blow into the water.


This helps reduce the amount of organic material entering the pool and protects your cover from sticks, branches, and sharp debris. It also makes closing day faster and easier when the time comes.


## 11. Start Planning for Closing, But Don’t Rush It


If you live in a colder climate, start thinking ahead so you have the right **[closing chemicals](https://lesliespool.com/pool-closing-chemicals/)** , **[cover accessories](https://lesliespool.com/pool-covers/)** , plugs, air pillows, and **[winterizing supplies](https://lesliespool.com/pool-closing-accessories/)** ready when it’s time. And don't forget to schedule a professional **[pool closing service](https://lesliespool.com/service)** with Leslie's!


The goal is to keep your pool clean, balanced, and protected until you’re actually ready to close. Closing too early can lead to algae if the water is still warm. Waiting too long can create problems if freezing temperatures arrive before the pool is prepared.


## Fall Pool Care Checklist


Use this quick checklist to keep your pool in great shape between summer and winter closing:


- Test and balance your water regularly
- Skim leaves and debris often
- Empty skimmer and pump baskets
- Brush walls, steps, and corners
- Vacuum the pool thoroughly
- Treat stains before they set
- Clean and inspect your filter
- Check equipment for leaks, noise, or poor flow
- Schedule a heater or heat pump tune-up
- Inspect your pool cover for damage
- Clean and store floats, toys, and accessories
- Replace worn maintenance tools
- Trim branches and clean the pool area
- Stock up on closing supplies before you need them
